chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created a people for faith, from which there is no decline; and He created a people for disbelief, from which there is no decline; and He created a people in between, and deposited faith in some of them. So if He wills to complete it for them, He completes it; and if He wills to deprive them of it, He deprives them of it; and so-and-so from them was with temporary faith.'

key_terms.لَا زَوَالَ لَهُ: From which there is no decline/cessation

ai.seo_question: What are the three categories of people regarding faith and disbelief in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia doctrine of divine decree by categorizing humanity into three groups: those predestined for permanent faith, those for permanent disbelief, and an intermediate group whose faith is contingent upon God's will. It specifically highlights the concept of 'temporary faith' (iman mu'ar) for the latter, illustrating that their spiritual state can be completed or revoked by God, reflecting the interplay between divine will and human agency. This perspective is significant in Shia theology as it balances predestination with the possibility of spiritual change, offering hope for those in the intermediate category.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I heard himasws saying: ‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Created a people for the Emān, there not being a decline for it, and Created a people for the Kufr (disbelief), there being no decline for it, and Created a people between that and Deposited the Emān in some of them. So if Heazwj so Desires Heazwj would Complete it for them, and if Heazwj so Desires Heazwj would Confiscate it from them; and so and so from them was with temporary Emān’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I heard either of the two Imams (a.s.) saying, ‘

Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has created a creature for belief and there is no transition in it. He has created a creature for disbelief and there is no transition in it. He has created a creature in between. He has deposited belief in certain individuals among them. If He wills to complete it for them He does so for them, and if He wishes to remove it from them He does so and so and so was of transient (belief) among them.’” (So and so is a reference to Muhammad ibn Miqlas al- Asadi al-Kufi)
